newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Bank of Taiwan issues US$200 mln FRNs in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Taiwan issues US$200 mln FRNs in Europe.

text.p: Bank of Taiwan, the island's top state-run bank, said on Thursday it had completed pricing for a US$200 million issue of floating rate notes and would list them formally on November 28 in Luxembourg.

"We just completed pricing for the FRNs, and with demand active, we got a satisfyingly low rate of LIBOR plus 11 basis points," a Bank of Taiwan executive told Reuters, asking that his name not be used.
The rate was lower than the executive's original estimate of LIBOR plus 13 to 15 basis points.
The five-year FRN issue was the first by a Taiwan bank and the rate was the lowest so far for any Taiwan firm's issue, the executive said.
"The smooth progress of this issue will help Taiwan firms gain confidence to issue more Eurobonds there," he said.
The bank first disclosed in September that it was planning a US$200 million issue of Eurobonds in Luxembourg.
